the scream|munch.title: Not the one screaming
the scream|munch.story: Munch described walking at sunset when he felt 'an infinite scream passing through nature'. So the figure isn't screaming; it is covering its ears against a scream it hears all around it.

the scream|munch.title: A blood-red sky
the scream|munch.story: The swirling red and orange sky has puzzled people for years. Some think Munch remembered the vivid sunsets seen across Europe after the Krakatoa volcano erupted in 1883; others think it simply shows how he felt.

the scream|munch.title: Tiny writing in the corner
the scream|munch.story: Faint pencil writing in the top left corner says it 'can only have been painted by a madman'. In 2021, experts confirmed the handwriting was Munch's own, likely added after critics questioned his mental health.

the scream|munch.title: Two figures walking away
the scream|munch.story: Behind the figure, two people stroll calmly along the railing. Munch wrote that his friends walked on while he stood trembling with anxiety, completely alone with the feeling.

judith slaying holofernes|gentileschi.title: Two women, working together
judith slaying holofernes|gentileschi.story: Unlike many earlier versions, Artemisia shows Judith and her servant acting together with strength and determination, not as fragile figures.

judith slaying holofernes|gentileschi.title: A painter who refused to be silenced
judith slaying holofernes|gentileschi.story: Artemisia Gentileschi was one of the most successful painters of her age and the first woman admitted to Florence's Academy of Fine Arts. Many see personal courage in this painting, made after she endured a public trial in which she accused her teacher of assault.

the horse fair|bonheur.title: A permit to wear trousers
the horse fair|bonheur.story: To sketch freely at the noisy Paris horse market, Rosa Bonheur obtained official permission from the police to wear trousers, which women were otherwise forbidden to do in public.

the horse fair|bonheur.title: Painted from life
the horse fair|bonheur.story: Bonheur spent about a year and a half making studies of real horses. The huge canvas made her famous across Europe and America.

the cradle|morisot.title: A sister watching
the cradle|morisot.story: The mother is Morisot's sister Edma, gazing at her sleeping baby. Edma had also been a painter, but gave it up after marriage.

the cradle|morisot.title: A see-through veil
the cradle|morisot.story: Look at the soft white curtain draped over the cradle. Morisot painted its transparency with light, quick strokes. She was the only woman among the founding group at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.

the childs bath|cassatt.title: Looking down from above
the childs bath|cassatt.story: We see the mother and child from above, with the floor tilting up toward us. Cassatt borrowed this unusual viewpoint from the Japanese prints she admired.

the childs bath|cassatt.title: Bold patterns
the childs bath|cassatt.story: The striped dress, the patterned rug and the painted jug create flat, decorative areas of pattern, another idea inspired by Japanese art.

marie antoinette with a rose|le brun.title: A safer portrait
marie antoinette with a rose|le brun.story: Shortly before this, Vigée Le Brun had painted the queen in a simple cotton dress, which caused a scandal. This formal portrait in silk, holding a rose, was made to calm the critics.
